uncited: NeRF-Based Reflectance Rendering is a technique that modifies the base color of a 3D object's surface by applying a neural network reflectance model.
It operates on points sampled from visible surfaces to account for view-dependent and light-dependent color variations.

It differs from standard NeRF rendering by focusing on surface-level reflectance modification rather than volumetric density and color estimation, building on [Surface Sampling for NeRF Rendering](14054-surface-sampling-for-nerf-rendering.md).
Initialize `buffer` of shape `(height, width, 3)` with zeros.
Identify visible surfaces from `object_3d` relative to `camera_position`.
Pass tensors through the `ObjectReflectanceNeRF` model (or `ReflectanceNeRF`) within a `torch.no_grad()` block to get `modified_colors`.
If $0 \le x < width$ and $0 \le y < height$, set `buffer[y, x] = modified_color`.
A variant that separates geometric/lighting feature encoding from color modification using a two-branch MLP architecture.
- Time complexity is dominated by the neural network inference for each sampled point.
